why: Trie plus DFS: a normal letter follows one child, but a '.' must try every child, so find becomes a depth-first search through the trie that stops at the first full match.
hints: With a hash set, how many words would '.' force you to try? What structure lets you explore all of them while sharing prefixes?
Store words in a trie. find(node, i): if pattern[i] is a letter, go to that child; if it is '.', try find on every child; at the end of the pattern require the end flag.
Recursive DFS returning as soon as one branch succeeds. Insert is O(L); find is O(L) without dots and bounded by the trie size with them.
pitfalls: A '.' matches exactly one letter, so lengths must match: 'ca' does not match 'cat'.
Reaching the end of the pattern is not enough; that node must end a word.
